The mechanics verification benchmark crate provides original fixtures for OpenPipeStress using elementary open mechanics with invented numeric values; they are verification aids only and encode no code-specific acceptance criteria, protected standards content, or professional approval claims.
INTERNAL_ASSERTION_EPSILON is the internal assertion tolerance constant set to 1.0e-9 for floating-point comparisons in benchmark validation.
PKG09_FIXTURE_UNIT_SYSTEM_REF identifies the fixture unit system as "PKG09-FIXTURE-UNITS-EXPLICIT-N-M-RAD-K".

REQUIRED_READINESS_TBD_MARKERS enumerates readiness items that must remain TBD: final tolerance policy, release thresholds, CI gate policy, benchmark publication scope, external validation claims, and professional reliance.

FORBIDDEN_RELIANCE_CLAIM_MARKERS lists prohibited reliance phrases (e.g. "code compliant", "approved for professional reliance", "certified for professional reliance", "sealed engineering") that must not appear in benchmark text.

CANONICAL_DIMENSIONS defines the allowed physical dimension identifiers for expected values, including length, mass, force, moment, pressure, stress, rotation, thermal_expansion_coefficient, second_moment_area, section_modulus, and TBD.

BenchmarkFamily enum classifies fixtures into families: Cantilever, Frame, StraightPipe, SupportBoundary, PrimitiveLoad, IntegratedLinearStatic, LoadToResultantIntegration, ThermalGrowth, ImposedDisplacement, and StiffnessTransform.
RedistributionStatus enum has the single variant PublicOriginal, marking fixtures as project-original public content.
ReviewDisposition enum has the single variant AcceptedInventedFixture, marking fixtures as reviewed and accepted as invented.
BenchmarkProvenance struct records fixture provenance: source_name, source_location, source_license, contributor, contributor_certification, redistribution_status, and review_disposition.

BenchmarkProvenance::public_original constructs provenance with source_name "OpenPipeStress original mechanics benchmark", license "project-original-public-content", and a certification that content was generated from elementary open mechanics and not copied from protected standards, commercial software examples, or proprietary data.

BenchmarkProvenance::is_publicly_usable returns true only when redistribution_status is PublicOriginal, review_disposition is AcceptedInventedFixture, name/location/license are non-empty, and the certification contains "not copied from protected standards".

FixtureUnitBasis struct records explicit fixture-local unit identifiers for length, force, moment, stress, area, second_moment_area, section_modulus, linear_stiffness, mass_per_length, acceleration, rotation, temperature_interval, dimensionless, and distributed load.

FixtureUnitBasis::is_explicit_fixture_basis returns true only when unit_system_ref equals PKG09_FIXTURE_UNIT_SYSTEM_REF, status is "fixture-local-explicit-units-no-conversions", core unit fields are non-empty, and the note states the unit catalog remains TBD.

FIXTURE_UNIT_BASIS constant fixes fixture units as length=m, force=N, moment=N-m, stress=Pa, area=m^2, second_moment_area=m^4, section_modulus=m^3, linear_stiffness=N/m, mass_per_length=kg/m, acceleration=m/s^2, rotation=rad, temperature_interval=K; explicit fixture-local units only with no conversion constants and project unit catalog remaining TBD.
ExpectedValue struct holds a named expected result: name, value (f64), unit, dimension, and an optional tolerance_policy.
MechanicsBenchmark struct aggregates a fixture: fixture_id, family, description, assumptions, provenance, unit_basis, and expected_values.
MechanicsBenchmark::tolerance_policy_is_unresolved returns true when every expected value has no tolerance_policy (all None), reflecting the unresolved tolerance policy.

MechanicsBenchmark::has_dimensioned_expected_values returns true when every expected value is finite, has a non-empty unit, and a dimension in CANONICAL_DIMENSIONS, and the unit basis is an explicit fixture basis.

LoadToResultantIntegrationResult struct captures node-1 UY displacement and RZ rotation, assembled node-0 UY force and RZ moment, and midspan shear-y and bending-z.
OrientedLoadToResultantIntegrationResult struct captures node-1 UX displacement and RZ rotation, assembled node-0 UX force and RZ moment, and midspan shear-y and bending-z.

StationSweepResultantIntegrationResult struct holds a vector of StationSweepResultant station resultants.

ThermalPressureAxialEffectsResult struct captures thermal axial force, pressure thrust force, total axial effect force, equivalent node-i/j axial loads, recovered local i/j axial forces, end and midspan axial forces, and a station sweep.

CanonicalAnalyticalPayloadSolverResult struct captures distributed-load and point-force counts, y_reference vector, assembled nodal forces/moments, support reactions, node-1 displacement and rotation, midspan resultants, recovery hook counts, and load-vector trace chains.

Fixture active_set_one_way_fixture: an invented one-way support activates from a positive trial reaction; expected state Active, residual norm 1.0, not converged, with a NonConvergence warning diagnostic.
Fixture gap_closure_fixture: an invented positive-clearance gap (0.25 mm) remains closed at its explicit clearance; expected state Active, no changed supports, residual 0.0, converged, no diagnostic.

Fixture lift_off_fixture: an invented lift-off support loses contact when the trial reaction reaches zero; expected state Inactive, residual 1.0, not converged, with a NonConvergence warning diagnostic.
Fixture friction_transition_fixture: an invented friction pair (coefficient 0.30) classifies one support as sticking and one as sliding; expected residual 0.0, converged, no diagnostic.
Friction limit is coefficient times positive normal reaction; the case uses invented normal and tangential reactions with no component catalog data.

Fixture unresolved_nonconvergence_fixture: an invented support remains changed at the configured iteration limit (4); expected state Active, residual 1.0, not converged, with a NonConvergence failure diagnostic and SolveFailed status.
Helper diagnostic_matches checks that absence of expected diagnostic implies empty diagnostics, otherwise that exactly one diagnostic matches the expected code and severity.
Test inventory_covers_required_nonlinear_families asserts the inventory has no missing required families and contains exactly five fixtures.
Test fixtures_are_public_original_and_unit_aware asserts each fixture is publicly usable, its provenance source artifact exists, has dimensioned observations, and unresolved tolerance policy.
Test active_set_gap_lift_off_and_friction_outcomes_are_deterministic asserts every fixture matches its expected outcome.
Test nonconvergence_fixture_reports_failure_diagnostic asserts the case does not converge, is blocked, and reports one NonConvergence failure diagnostic mentioning non-convergence after 4 iterations.
Test expected_reports_preserve_warning_and_failure_statuses asserts the active-set warning report is SolvedWithWarnings (not blocked) and the non-convergence report is SolveFailed (blocked).

The mechanics hand-calculation notes support DEL-09-01, the mechanics benchmark suite.

All mechanics hand-calc numeric values are invented for public verification fixtures derived from elementary open mechanics; they are not protected standards, commercial examples, proprietary values, code-specific acceptance criteria, or professional approval evidence.
For mechanics hand-calcs, final tolerance policy, release thresholds, CI gate policy, benchmark publication scope, external validation claims, and professional reliance remain TBD.

Mechanics hand-calc notes use explicit fixture-local unit identifiers mapping quantity families to units and canonical dimensions (e.g., length m, force N, moment N-m, stress Pa, second moment of area m^4, section modulus m^3, linear stiffness N/m).
The project unit catalog and conversion constants remain TBD for the mechanics hand-calc notes.
The mechanics benchmark crate source inventory is mirrored in the README so each fixture has an explicit public-original hand-calculation note.
The mechanics fixture inventory maps fixture IDs to their hand-calculation note files (e.g., MECH-CANTILEVER-TIP-FORCE to cantilever_tip_force.md).

The validation/witness/tools package provides validation-local formal witness tooling.
witness_validator.py is a CLI tool that validates and renders validation-local OpenMath calculation witnesses.
ROOT is resolved as the repository root three parents above the tool file.
The default witness path is validation/witness/fixtures/tp_phys_015_section_property_stress_witness.json.
The witness schema is located at validation/witness/schemas/openmath_calculation_witness.schema.json.
Decimal arithmetic context precision is set to 50 digits for witness evaluation.

Physical dimensions are encoded as (length, force) integer-exponent tuples: dimensionless (0,0), length (1,0), force (0,1), moment (1,1), stress (-2,1), area (2,0), section_modulus (3,0), second_moment_area (4,0).
Supported OpenMath arith1 operators are: plus, minus, times, divide, power.
WitnessError is raised when a formal witness is invalid or generated artifacts are stale.
QuantityValue is a frozen dataclass holding a Decimal value, unit string, dimension tuple, and dimension name.
FormulaEvaluation is a frozen dataclass holding formula_id, display, expression, and a QuantityValue.
Comparison is a frozen dataclass holding formula_id, result_id, witness_value, ops_value, abs_delta, tolerance, and a passed flag.
WitnessEvaluation is a frozen dataclass holding witness_id, witness_sha256, formula_evaluations, and comparisons.
load_json reads and parses a UTF-8 JSON file from a path.
canonical_sha256 computes the SHA-256 hex digest over the witness serialized as canonical JSON with sorted keys and compact separators.
repo_path resolves a path against ROOT when it is not absolute.
decimal_text formats a Decimal as fixed-point text, returning '0' for zero.
dimension_name maps a dimension vector to its name, falling back to 'derived<vector>' for unknown vectors.
validate_schema validates the witness against the Draft 2020-12 JSON schema and raises WitnessError on the first error.
quantity_from_binding constructs a QuantityValue from a binding's quantity, reading decimal, unit, and dimension.
arith_result computes the QuantityValue result of an arith1 operator over argument QuantityValues, raising WitnessError for unsupported operators.
For arith1.plus and arith1.minus, all argument dimensions must match the first argument's dimension or a dimension mismatch error is raised.
arith1.minus requires exactly two arguments.
arith1.times multiplies argument decimals and adds their dimension exponents component-wise.
arith1.divide requires exactly two arguments and subtracts the divisor's dimension exponents from the dividend's.
arith1.power requires exactly two arguments.
The arith1.power exponent must be dimensionless and an integer, otherwise WitnessError is raised.
arith1.power multiplies the base dimension exponents by the integer exponent.
evaluate_openmath recursively evaluates an OpenMath node into a QuantityValue given bound values, formulas, and an evaluation stack.
An OMV node resolves to a bound value, else recurses into a formula of the same name; an unknown variable raises WitnessError.
A formula graph cycle is detected when an OMV name already appears on the evaluation stack, raising WitnessError.
OMI and OMF nodes evaluate to dimensionless QuantityValues with unit '1'.
An OMS node is supported only for nums1.pi, which must be present in bound values; other symbols raise WitnessError.
An OMA node's operator must be an OMS in the arith1 content dictionary; otherwise the operator is unsupported.
An OMA node evaluates its arguments recursively and applies arith_result with the operator name.
evaluate_formula evaluates a formula by id, memoizing into values and detecting cycles via the stack.
A formula's evaluated dimension must match its expected_dimension or WitnessError is raised.
evaluate_formula stores the result with the formula's expected_unit and expected_dimension.
display_map builds an id-to-display lookup over the witness constants, inputs, and formulas sections.
expression_for renders an OpenMath node into a human-readable infix expression string using the display map.
expression_for formats operators as parenthesized infix: plus and times join args, minus and divide are binary, power uses caret notation.
flatten_results flattens an OPS result export's result_envelope result_sets into a result_id-keyed map.
evaluate_witness validates the schema, binds constants and inputs, evaluates all formulas, and compares outputs against the OPS result export.
evaluate_witness loads the OPS result export from the witness result_export path resolved against the repo root.
A missing OPS result id for an output raises WitnessError.
An output's witness dimension name must match the OPS result dimension or WitnessError is raised.
Each output comparison passes only when the absolute delta between witness and OPS values is within the output's abs_tolerance_decimal.
An OPS result mismatch exceeding tolerance raises WitnessError reporting witness value, OPS value, delta, and tolerance.
render_markdown evaluates the witness and renders a Markdown report of provenance, inputs, formula evaluation, result comparison, and boundary.
The generated Markdown declares it is generated from the machine-readable witness artifact and must not be edited as the authoritative calculation source.
The Markdown reports the witness SHA-256 over canonical JSON as a sha256: prefixed value.

The witness is mechanics-only software verification evidence: it does not compare to allowables, classify code stress categories, apply fatigue rules, use SIF/flexibility factors, certify, seal, authenticate, approve, or declare code compliance.
mathml_for recursively renders an OpenMath node into MathML lines with indentation.
An OMV renders as <ci>, OMI/OMF as <cn>, and nums1.pi as <pi/> in MathML.
An OMA renders as a MathML <apply> with the operator element and recursively rendered arguments.
render_mathml evaluates the witness and renders an ops-witness-mathml document containing per-formula MathML with witness id and SHA-256 attributes.
Each formula's MathML is wrapped in semantics with an eq apply and an OpenMath-JSON annotation of the formula id.
assert_generated_artifacts_current raises WitnessError if the on-disk generated Markdown or MathML differs from the freshly rendered output.
write_generated_artifacts regenerates and writes the Markdown and MathML artifacts to their witness-declared paths, creating parent directories.
parse_args defines a CLI accepting an optional witness path plus --write-generated and --check-generated flags.
The witness positional argument defaults to the TP-PHYS-015 pilot witness.
main loads the witness, evaluates it, optionally writes or checks generated artifacts, and returns exit code 1 on WitnessError else 0.
The module is executable as a script, exiting with main's return code.
